# bugs #2672: mcs51: peephole rules 107 and 200.a remove the last entries of a jump table

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/2672/
- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17193
- Recommended action: Apply and close. Confirm the cost in code size: 2 or 3 bytes in some tables and 2 bytes for some jumps outside of tables.
- Patch: [bugs-2672.patch](../../patches/bugs-2672.patch), commit [`5d1671556`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/5d167155618c1b6003efd3c5479307c96c480c94). Applies to r17193 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

On r17176 the file `sp_sfc_operation_handler.c` of the attached project gets wrong code with the
ticket's options `--model-large --opt-code-speed`. The float expression and `expf` are not
involved. The `switch` on `sfc_state` in `error_check` has case values 0 to 8, and its jump table
has entries for 0 to 6 only. For the value 8, the jump arrives three bytes after the start of the
first block of the switch body. A harness that calls `sfc_operation_handler` in ucsim with that
state gets `ERROR_INV_DC_OFFSET` where `ERROR_INV_OVL` is correct. In the medium model the call
does not return, and `main` starts again and again. Both models are correct with `--no-peep`.

The option is not needed for a smaller switch. In the function `twoLast` of the patch's test, the
case values 4 and 3 share the first block of the switch body. On r17176 `twoLast (4)` skips the
first instruction of that block in the small, medium, large, and huge models and with
`--stack-auto`.

## Cause

`genJumpTab` in `src/mcs51/gen.c` emits a table of `ljmp` instructions for a switch with at most 7
table entries, and with at most 16 under `--opt-code-speed`. When the block of the highest case
values is the first block of the switch body, the last entries jump to the label that follows the
table.

Rule 107 in `src/mcs51/peeph.def` replaces `ljmp %1` before `%1:` with the label. Rules 200.a and
200.b do this for `sjmp`, and the entries are `sjmp` instructions after one of the rules 260 has
converted the table. The only condition of the three rules was `labelRefCountChange(%1 -1)`, so
the optimizer removed the last entry of such a table. The code is still correct then, because the
index of that entry selects the address that follows the table. After each rule marked `restart`
the optimizer goes through the rules again, and each pass removed one more entry with the same
target. After two removals the highest index selects an address inside the first instruction of
the block.

## Fix

The patch adds `notInJumpTable()` to rules 107, 200.a, and 200.b. The condition is false for the
lines of a `JUMPTABLE` iCode. [r16836](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/16836/) added it to
rule 257.c for bug #4066, in which a rule changed the size of a table entry.

## Decision

- Tables whose last entry jumps to the label after the table keep that entry, which is 3 bytes
  for `ljmp` and 2 bytes for `sjmp`. A condition that allows the removal of the last entry only
  was not tried.
- `notInJumpTable` is also false for lines that do not have an iCode, and replacements that join
  lines of several iCodes produce such lines. The three rules now leave a redundant jump there,
  outside of jump tables. In the regression suite for the small model, 4 tests grow by 2 bytes
  each: bug-2890326 and the GCC torture tests 20071011-1, 20141022-1, and pr49161. The
  alternative is a `notInJumpTable` that returns true for these lines. That changes shared code
  and changes when rule 257.c is applied. It was not tried.
- Rule 200.b got the condition because it has the pattern of rule 200.a with two labels. A test
  case that fails through rule 200.b was not found.

## Verification

The patch adds `support/regression/tests/bug-2672.c`. With the r17192 compiler the test fails 3 of
its 42 assertions in each of the six mcs51 configurations of the regression suite. With the
condition on rule 107 alone, the assertion for the function `padded` still fails in each of the
six, because rule 200.a removes entries after the table has become an `sjmp` table. With the patch
the test passes. The project of the ticket was not compiled again with the patch.

With the patch series of this report up to this patch applied to r17192, the regression suite
passes for host, the six mcs51 configurations, stm8, and ucz80. In the two stack-auto
configurations, `printf_large.c` of the library gets a stack frame that is one byte larger than
without this patch, and about 70 tests that link it grow by 8 to 40 bytes. The rules of this patch
do not cause that by what they match. For that file, r17192 without any patch gives three
different results when `--peep-file` adds files of 0 to 40 rules that never match, and one command
line always gives one result. The cause was not investigated.
